root_cause.statement: With `--tool-call-parser qwen3_xml` and no `--reasoning-parser`, the model's single legitimate `</think>` is silently swallowed by the combined Qwen3 parser engine. `qwen3_xml` maps to Qwen3EngineToolParser, an adapter over the combined Qwen3Parser ParserEngine that owns BOTH reasoning and tool-call grammar. When wired as a tool parser only, the adapter runs that engine in ParserState.CONTENT, where the transition (ParserState.CONTENT, THINK_END) -> (CONTENT, no events) fires. That transition exists only to absorb a *duplicate* `</think>` after a separate reasoning parser has already ended reasoning; with no reasoning parser attached it instead eats the model's first and only `</think>`. Because `</think>` is a registered lexer/token-id terminal it is never emitted as literal text, and the reasoning and answer text on either side both flow through as content -- so deliberation is concatenated into `content` ahead of the answer with the only boundary removed and no `reasoning_content`.
root_cause.mechanism: Wiring: ParserManager.get_parser builds a DelegatingParser with reasoning_parser=None and tool_parser=Qwen3ParserToolAdapter (tool_parsers/__init__.py:169 maps qwen3_xml -> Qwen3EngineToolParser; the matching reasoning half is reasoning name 'qwen3' -> Qwen3ParserReasoningAdapter, reasoning/__init__.py:122, which was NOT selected). NON-STREAMING (chat_completion_full_generator -> DelegatingParser.parse, abstract_parser.py:785): extract_reasoning() sees _reasoning_parser is None and returns (None, full_output) (abstract_parser.py:390) -- so reasoning_content=None and the FULL output (reasoning + '</think>' + answer) is passed to the tool parser via _extract_tool_calls -> extract_tool_calls -> Qwen3ParserToolAdapter.extract_tool_calls (adapters.py:158) -> ParserEngine.extract_tool_calls_from_content (parser_engine.py:556) which calls _single_pass_parse(..., initial_state=ParserState.CONTENT). In CONTENT: reasoning text -> content_events[CONTENT]=TEXT_CHUNK -> content; '</think>' terminal -> StreamingParserEngine._on_terminal finds transition (CONTENT, THINK_END) and _apply_transition emits its (empty) events tuple -> nothing emitted -> tag dropped (streaming_parser_engine.py:312-356,382-436); answer -> TEXT_CHUNK -> content. Result content = reasoning+answer, '</think>' gone. STREAMING (parse_delta, abstract_parser.py:801): with _reasoning_parser is None, state.reasoning_ended is set True up-front (line 815-818), _in_reasoning_phase()=False so the reasoning branch is skipped, and _in_tool_call_phase()=True (line 743) routes every delta to Qwen3ParserToolAdapter.extract_tool_calls_streaming, which calls engine.initialize_streaming(initial_state=ParserState.CONTENT) (adapters.py:178). The '</think>' token (id 248069) is pre-lexed as THINK_END by the token-id scanner and hits the same (CONTENT, THINK_END) drop transition; reasoning/answer stream out as content deltas. Both paths therefore drop '</think>' and merge reasoning into content, finish_reason=stop (no truncation). NOTE / correction to the report's pointer: the config's initial_state is REASONING when thinking=True, but the tool-parser adapter overrides it to CONTENT (parser_engine.py:571 and adapters.py:178); so the operative culprit is specifically the SECOND transition, (ParserState.CONTENT, THINK_END) with empty events (qwen3.py:130-135), not (REASONING, THINK_END). Had the engine actually run in REASONING here, the reasoning would instead be parsed into delta.reasoning and then DISCARDED by extract_tool_calls_from_content (which drops the reasoning return value), which does not match the observed 'merged into content' symptom -- confirming the CONTENT-state path.

proposed_fix.summary: Two layers. PRIMARY (root fix): treat qwen3_xml as the combined engine it is -- when a ParserEngine-backed tool parser that owns a reasoning phase is selected and no reasoning parser is configured, auto-attach the engine's matching reasoning adapter (or, at minimum, fail-loud/warn at startup). That restores reasoning_content and makes '</think>' a proper REASONING_END boundary. DEFENSIVE (narrow): make the (CONTENT, THINK_END) 'absorb duplicate' transition fire only for a genuine duplicate -- i.e. only after a REASONING_END has actually been emitted this parse; otherwise emit the literal '</think>' as content instead of dropping it, so a mis-configured tool-only setup never silently deletes the client's boundary marker.

changes.what: In get_parser, when tool_parser_cls is a ParserEngine adapter that owns reasoning (e.g. exposes a paired reasoning_parser_cls, as set by make_adapters) and reasoning_parser_cls is None, auto-select that paired reasoning adapter (qwen3_xml -> reasoning 'qwen3'/Qwen3ParserReasoningAdapter). Guard so an explicitly-different reasoning parser is respected.

If auto-attach is undesirable, emit a startup warning/validation error when a combined-engine tool parser is chosen without a reasoning parser, so the silent reasoning-into-content merge cannot happen unnoticed.

Defensive fallback: replace the unconditional (ParserState.CONTENT, THINK_END) -> (CONTENT, ()) drop with logic that only drops when reasoning already ended this parse; otherwise emit THINK_END's literal text as a content chunk (or route it as REASONING_END). Lines 130-135.

If the defensive approach is taken, thread a 'reasoning_already_ended' flag into the transition application so the drop is conditional (the engine already tracks _reasoning_ended in ParserEngine._events_to_delta).

evidence.note: (REASONING, THINK_END) emits REASONING_END without re-emitting the tag; (CONTENT, THINK_END) has an empty events tuple -> the 'absorb duplicate </think>' silent-drop transition.

qwen3_config sets initial_state=REASONING when thinking else CONTENT; thinking derived only from chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking (qwen3.py:226) -- never consulted here is whether a reasoning parser is attached.

_on_terminal: terminal WITH a transition -> _apply_transition (empty events => nothing emitted => tag dropped); terminal WITHOUT a transition -> _emit_for_state (literal text emitted as content). This is why '</think>' vanishes but a tag lacking a CONTENT-state transition would not.

Tool adapter: non-streaming routes to extract_tool_calls_from_content; streaming calls initialize_streaming(initial_state=ParserState.CONTENT) -> engine runs in CONTENT, overriding the config's REASONING initial_state.

extract_tool_calls_from_content runs _single_pass_parse with initial_state=ParserState.CONTENT and discards the reasoning return value -- confirming that in this path reasoning is treated as CONTENT (merged), matching the symptom.
Non-streaming: _reasoning_parser is None => extract_reasoning returns (None, model_output); the full output incl. '</think>' is handed to the tool parser and reasoning_content stays None.
Streaming: _reasoning_parser is None => state.reasoning_ended=True up-front, reasoning phase skipped, every delta routed to the tool parser (CONTENT-state engine).

qwen3_xml -> Qwen3EngineToolParser (combined engine, tool half); reasoning 'qwen3' -> Qwen3ParserReasoningAdapter (same engine, reasoning half). Correct config for this model is --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --reasoning-parser qwen3; omitting the reasoning parser is what triggers the bug.

Default generation prompt opens an unclosed '<think>\n' every turn (enable_thinking!=false), so the model closes it with '</think>' before answering -> Core Question 2 premise holds; report arm B (completions, no parser) showing 5/5 '</think>' corroborates the model reliably emits it.

follow_ups: Decide auto-attach vs fail-loud for combined-engine tool parsers missing their reasoning half; auto-attach is more user-friendly but changes behavior silently for anyone who intentionally ran tool-only.

Audit the other combined ParserEngine parsers (deepseek_v32/v4, glm47_moe, minimax_m2, nemotron_v3, seed_oss, gemma4, kimi_k2, inkling, mistral) for the identical tool-parser-only '</think>'-style boundary-drop, since they share the (CONTENT, <reasoning-end>) absorb-duplicate pattern and the same adapter CONTENT-start.
Consider surfacing reasoning_content even in tool-only mode by having extract_tool_calls_from_content optionally return reasoning rather than discarding it.
